logline: Following the broken pieces to a night shore, the poet finds his own heart and then his own two hands lying where he left them, puts each back on with care, and says 'nevermore' until he can say 'Now go.'
reading:
Nevermore is the recovery that follows 03's ruin, built as two 'What if I follow' journeys. In the first he follows the trail of broken pieces to a shore of wildfire ash and sea-floor debris. The waves fold to whispers, the wind mutes the trees, and in that silence he finds 'a throbbing heart left at the midlife corner', familiar and his. He lifts it with care and puts it back in place. 'Nevermore' here is a vow, not a lament.

The turn is 'What if I follow this reclaimed heart', the same sentence with a new guide. In the second journey he follows his heart into a moonlit field where puzzle pieces of faith scatter like mustard seed, golden plants turn to face him, and weeds fall back into the shadows where memory hides. Then the clouds put out the stars and he searches bare ground for his two hands, 'hands that once could touch dusk after dusk'. He puts them back on 'with the care of my future at stake.' The confession 'I've wanted the world and lost my soul' gives way to 'I'll be alright', and the poem ends on two words: nevermore, then Now go.
motifs: 'What if I follow': two journeys, the trail and then the reclaimed heart
the heart found outside the body and put back in place
hands detached and re-seated: his own construction restored
silence as a condition: waves folded to whispers, muted trees
mustard seed and puzzle pieces of faith, scattered
golden blooms turning to face him; weeds recoiling into shadow
the deepest darkness, where the stars are muted, as the place of hard work

light_and_texture: Moonlight from high frame-left as a single cool key, with the heart as the only warm source until the field turns gold. In 04.5 light comes from a code-drawn circle around his reach and nothing else. Cards: black track-jacket cut from black corrugated board with the red piping as a painted kraft strip, sunglasses as a separate glossy black card, and the ash shore as grey pastel rubbed over kraft. The heart is a small glossy-varnished card that reads wet against the matte world. The hands should show their brass brads and eyelets clearly, so that putting them back on is literally re-seating a joint.

gaps: A figure-free ash-covered night shore with tambourine pieces and chapel remnants: the shore plates either carry a figure (gen_c77b296bbf, gen_306845943e) or are a stair (view_097).
The red_black_sunglasses puppet painted at all: pack and action sheet are blank layouts, and the poem's main pose, a walk with hands in pockets, has no cell.
Torso cards with a cut chest hollow (heartless) and a heart-seated version.
The detachable hands as props: hand_L and hand_R lying palm-down in grit, dusty, with visible eyelets.
The heart prop: a small anatomical heart with beat and glow states (generated hearts are neon or held by other figures).
Turning golden blooms with replacement heads (closed, open-away, open-facing) and recoiling weeds.
A 'deepest darkness' plate: the field under cloud with only a lit patch of bare ground.
Archive of hands working soil at dusk and of an anatomical heart being placed; only fragments so far.

fx.how: Cut a heart-shaped window in the torso card and key gen_d877af5eab or plain night sky behind it, so the world shows through him.
Code path: the heart card rises from the sand on a slow ease, with a 2% scale pulse at the poem's own spoken rhythm, then snaps into the chest brad with one frame of glow.
Alternate the resting and swollen heart cards; at the same time a thin red oscilloscope trace (Sound Waves and Their Sources, 1933) pulses in a pane.
Slow the water plate to a near-stop and lay three paper wave-lines that flatten one by one.
Hold a frame of Wind in Trees 8 (2007) or gen_366225426b as a freeze, with the wind sound dropped out on the same frame.
Swap each bloom card closed → open-away → open-facing in a ripple that follows his walk.
Weed cards bend back on their base brads and a soft black gradient slides over them.
Code particles sampled from the painted seed swatch, falling under gravity with a little gold glint.
Stars masked out one by one by sliding cloud cards, then the exposure crushed until only the reach-of-touch circle remains.
A code-drawn soft circle of moonlight centred on his torso brad that tracks him, and widens when the hands are restored.
Three to five raven cards on looping paths with a 4-card wing cycle; for wide shots cut in Blackbirds on a Wire (2007).

passage.keep: The lowered head is right for 'What if I follow this reclaimed heart': his hands are still gone and his eyes are behind glasses, so only the head can carry it. The Snow Queen (1959) answers 'follow your heart to where it needs you' so literally that it feels like an instruction, and it sets up 'Now go'.
passage.better: Don't open the archive in the night sea patch, since water reads faint. Stage it on view_097: POET on the lit stairs with the tall stone wall beside him, and the Snow Queen opening on the wall face as a large vertical pane. Put a faint warm glow in the chest hollow card under his lowered chin so the head-down reads as looking at the heart. Swap to a 'down' replacement head, not a rotation.
alt_lines: 04_L09 'and it used to be mine. I'll lift it with care': no hands, so head lowers and the heart rises; The Unique Contribution (1959) red heart opens in the stone wall of view_097.

04_L13 'The plants in a golden hue bloom and face toward me': head lifts (awe) in gen_ca6878be91; Accidents Don't Just Happen's yellow flowers open in the window frame of gen_366225426b at the field's edge.
04_L17 'to search the bare ground for two hands': empty sleeves held out, wrists bare; Victory Gardens hands with seed open on the lit soil circle (bright, large).
04_L19 'and they too used to be mine': hand held out, the newly seated hand_L turned palm-up; Victory Gardens hands (arch_ea553edf-9921) in the gen_366225426b frame.
04_L25 'in this still muted tree in night garden': hands relaxed, head level; Wind in Trees 8 (2007), frozen, opens inside the gen_366225426b frame.

ideas: Heart and line: The Unique Contribution's red heart (1959) and the Sound Waves and Their Sources (1933) trace intercut as the heart card beats in the sand. When it seats in his chest the trace steadies.
Seeds into hands: Victory Gardens' seed pouring into a palm plays on the lit soil circle just before the hand cards are found, so the archive hands lead the puppet to his own.
Ash and fire: Watershed wildfire (1958) burning low in the stone wall of view_097 while ash particles drift over POET walking with hands in pockets. The fire is expired by the time he passes.
Debris from the floor: The Photographer (1948) white driftwood in still water as the far layer, with sea_debris cards washed up in front and 03's tambourine pieces strung along the line.
Turning field: in gen_ca6878be91 a row of golden_bloom cards flips to face him one by one as he walks; the gen_bad0cf8d7a gold points fade up in the background.
Deepest dark: cloud cards slide over gen_ca6878be91's Milky Way until black, then cut to Long Distance (1941)'s near-black frame and back to the single lit circle with two hands in it.
Ravens on the climb: Blackbirds on a Wire (2007) as the opening of 04.3a, then the birds lift off the wire and become raven cards flying up the view_071 path ahead of him.
Now go: final still in gen_366225426b, with POET seen small and from behind in the frame's foreground, hands at his sides. On 'Now go' he takes one step and the next poem opens.
